title: What is known about 1RB0RB_0LC1RA_1RD1LC_1LA1LE_1LF0LD_---0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_0LC1RA_1RD1LC_1LA1LE_1LF0LD_---0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the moves an excursion is made of, the only way the machine can halt (0 0 D> 1, reached at the left end when a pass meets an odd lead block), and that step 589,506 starts the third epoch on the tape P (01)^520. Simulator laws, checked on small counters and extrapolated, give epoch 3 a length of about 3.6·1026 excursions (1053 steps) and predict that neither epoch 3 nor epoch 4 ends in a halt; beyond epoch 4 nothing is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 45,812 cells have been visited and 27,548 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.465).

claims.title: The moves of an excursion
claims.text: Twelve runs proved for every value of the variables and every surrounding tape: the A/B sweeps (11 ↔ 01), the D/E pass, the two ends of a tail block, the two left-going zigzag rounds and the two right-going rounds.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: 0 0 D> 1 halts two steps later (halt_00); a pass into the leftmost block halts if that block is odd (lead_odd) and otherwise turns right and extends the tape by one cell (lead_even).

claims.title: The start of epoch 3
claims.text: After 589,506 steps from blank tape the tape is P (01)^520 with the head in state A on the blank cell to its right (P a fixed 106-cell word).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>18</sup> steps
claims.text: The macro simulator (2-cell blocks, run-length stacks, 128-bit step counter) runs 10<sup>18</sup> steps from blank without a halt; the run is still in epoch 3.

claims.title: The epoch-3 law on small counters
claims.text: From P (01)^m, the number E(m) of excursions to the next left record satisfies E(m+12) = 4E(m)+2 for m = 12…87; for m = 4+12t, E = (14·4t−2)/3 and the epoch ends without a halt with E+1 trailing 10 pairs.

claims.title: Epoch 3 lasts about 3.6·10<sup>26</sup> excursions and does not halt
claims.text: The law extrapolated to m = 520 (t = 43): E = 361,065,844,791,569,246,845,577,898 excursions, roughly 10<sup>53</sup> steps, ending with N ≡ 7 (mod 12) trailing pairs.

claims.title: Epoch 4 does not halt
claims.text: With the trailing pairs of an epoch-3 end replaced by N₂ pairs (N₂ ≤ 30, t = 1…4) the next epoch halts exactly when N₂ ≡ 2 (mod 12) (t ≥ 2); the real N is ≡ 7. Epoch 4 then lasts about 4<sup>N/12</sup> excursions.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof of non-halting would need the excursion as a proved macro step, the countdown laws as theorems, and the residue test at every level of the tower; a halt, if any, would come after epoch 4, beyond 4<sup>10<sup>25</sup></sup> steps.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB0RB_0LC1RA_1RD1LC_1LA1LE_1LF0LD_---0LA/py/epochs.py epoch4 16,28 1,2,7,14     # which epoch-4 counters halt

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine counts down in base 4, and each countdown is exponentially longer than the last: the third one, which starts at step 589,506, lasts about 10<sup>53</sup> steps, and the fourth about 4<sup>3·10<sup>25</sup></sup> excursions. It can only stop at the end of a countdown, and only if a remainder comes out right.

facts.text: The only way to halt; it can happen only at the left end of the tape.
Epoch 3 starts on the tape P (01)^520, proved in Lean.
Excursions in epoch 3, from the law E(m+12) = 4E(m)+2; it ends without a halt.
Epoch 4 is predicted not to halt; nothing is known beyond it.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.465).
After 109 steps the tape spans 45,812 cells (44 left of the start, 33,809 right), with a density of 1s of 0.601.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: One excursion
html: Watch the head each time it stands in state A on the blank cell right of the tape. The tape is then always a row of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. From there it makes an excursion: B turns it around, a D/E pass runs left through the last block turning each 1 1 into 0 1, and then the head zigzags further left in rounds of 8 + 2j cells, each rewriting a stretch like 0101 01 12j into 00 1101 12j 10. When the word left of the head no longer fits a round, it comes back right, flipping pairs (11 ↔ 01) on the way, and ends one pair 1 0 further right than it started.

Every one of these moves is a Lean theorem for all lengths and every surrounding tape (lean/Rules.lean). What is not proved is that an excursion always decomposes into exactly these moves.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading a 0. F is entered only from E reading a 0, and E only from D reading a 1, so a halt is exactly the pattern 0 0 D> 1 (halt_00). Inside the tape the D/E pass always meets a single 0 and turns into a zigzag instead. The pattern can occur at the left end: when a pass runs through the leftmost block of the tape and reaches blank tape.

leftmost blockwhat happenstheorem
odd, 12a+1halt, 2a+2 steps laterlead_odd
even, 12a+2the head turns right; the tape gains a cell on the leftlead_even
So the run is cut into epochs by the moments the head reaches a new cell on the far left, and the question is whether the leftmost block is ever odd at one of those moments.

sections.heading: Each epoch is a base-4 countdown
html: Within an epoch the excursions go to different depths in a pattern like a base-4 counter: most stay shallow, one in four goes a fixed step deeper. Epoch 3 starts at step 589,506 on the tape P (01)520 (proved in Lean, epoch3_start). Starting the machine on P (01)m for small m and counting the excursions E(m) to the next left record gives a clean law:

E(m+12) = 4E(m)+2 holds for every m from 12 to 87 in the simulator; twelve more pairs are one more base-4 digit. Extrapolated to the real m = 520, epoch 3 lasts about 3.6·1026 excursions (roughly 1053 steps) and ends without a halt, leaving N = E+1 pairs 1 0 on the right, with N ≡ 7 (mod 12).

sections.heading: Epoch 4 and the tower
html: The end of epoch 3 looks like core (10)N 110, and those N pairs are the counter of epoch 4. Replacing N by small values N₂ shows the same law one level up (E₄(N₂+12) = 4E₄(N₂)+2) and a residue test: the epoch ends in a halt exactly when N₂ ≡ 2 (mod 12). The real N is ≡ 7, so epoch 4 should end without halting, after about 4N/12 ≈ 43·1025 excursions.

The same thing then repeats with a far larger counter, and a residue test at each level decides whether the machine stops. Nobody has worked out the test for epoch 5. This is the shape of a tower: the machine probably runs for an unimaginably long time, and whether it ever halts is open.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html: Proved in Lean by the kernel: the twelve moves of an excursion, the halting pattern and the two left-end outcomes. Proved with native_decide: the run reaches the start of epoch 3. Measured with a simulator: no halt in 1018 steps, the epoch law on small counters, the epoch-4 residues. Extrapolated (heuristic): the length and outcome of epochs 3 and 4. Missing for a proof: the tape grammar and the excursion as one proved macro step, the countdown law as a theorem, and the residue test at every level.

family: Tower of base-4 countdowns with a residue test at each epoch end
summary: Each epoch is a base-4 countdown on the excursion depth whose length is exponential in the counter it starts with (epoch 3: P (01)^520, about 3.6·10^26 excursions); halting is only possible at an epoch end, when the lead block is odd. Simulator laws predict epochs 3 and 4 end without halting; epoch 4 already has about 4^(3·10^25) excursions.
